title: TPO Seams in Texas Heat
description: A TPO roof in Texas often fails at the weld while the field still looks white and new. Heat, foot traffic, and a weak seam are the usual story.
html:
TPO looks simple from the parking lot. A white sheet, a few seams, boxes for the air conditioners. The sheet can still look clean while a weld has opened. On a Texas building the seam is where we look first, because the heat that makes the roof a good idea is also what tests every weld.

A weld is only as good as the day it was made

TPO seams are hot-air welded. The two sheets become one piece when the temperature, the speed, and the pressure were right. A weld that was too cool can look closed and open years later, often along the same line, often near a wall or a unit where the welder had to slow down and work by hand. We probe seams. A visual pass from the hatch is not an inspection.

Foot traffic from technicians adds the second insult. Pads should exist where people walk. Without them, the membrane scuffs, the seam sees abrasion, and a screw or a tool dropped on a July afternoon starts a leak you will meet in the next storm. The field membrane can still be thick enough. The seam is the hinge.

Repair, coat, or replace

An open seam with a sound sheet around it is a weld repair. A roof that is opening in many places, shrinking at the perimeter, or chalking through is not a tube of sealant. A coating can make sense on a tired but attached membrane, which is the conversation on our coatings and restoration page. A sheet that has lost its welds across the building is a replacement. We will say which one the probe found. We will not coat a roof that is already coming apart at the seams to buy a year.

If the leak shows up under a seam line on the ceiling, tell us that. It saves a lap around the building. Call (281) 541-0027 or request a commercial inspection.
